reasoning: The pipeline's close rule states that a shown result closes the work and the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery. A row whose definition of done names his eye is describing one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserve for him — a taste call, a trade-off no artifact settles, or a still-open change to the definition of correct — never an ordinary buildable result a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms was delivered. Here the outcome is decidable without making the person the checker: render-board.sh regenerates board.html from PLAN.md, every declared row appears under its own state, tests/test_board_matches_the_canon.py passes against the generated page, and the closing check reached the product on real data — the page as it renders. Nothing in the result is a matter of preference and no fork is open, so the acceptance line as written does not name one of the reserved cases; it is a stale eye-gate on an ordinary delivery. The pipeline shows the result and closes the checkpoint and row in the same step, without waiting for his attention. If he disagrees after seeing it, that disagreement is a new fact and becomes its own task; the closed row stays closed. Nothing here is irreversible outside git, so rule 12's own stop-before-acting ground is not engaged.
